title: Théorie de Kumer ? + note Alexandre (bi tenseur…) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This page continues the elementary lecture-style material on classifying spaces begun on the previous page. Thm 1 there characterized a universal principal π-covering E→B (π discrete) as one with E contractible. Thm 2 here states that for every discrete group π a universal π-bundle exists. Equivalently, a classifying space Bπ = K(π,1) exists, and it is unique up to unique isomorphism in the homotopy category (as a pair with its universal covering class). Grothendieck then introduces the Borel construction (homotopy quotient). For a space X with a π-action, form E_π ×_π X = (E_π × X)/π. It has two projections: one to B_π = E_π/π, which is a fibration with fibre X, and one to the naive quotient X/π. The long exact homotopy sequence of the fibration X → E_π×_π X → B_π, together with π_2(B_π)=0 and π_1(B_π)=π, gives the following: 0 → π_1(X) → π_1(X,π) → π → π_0(X). Here π_1(X,π) := π_1(E_π ×_π X) is the equivariant (orbifold) fundamental group. When X is connected (π_0(X)=1, as noted under the sequence), π_1(X,π) is an extension of π by π_1(X). The next page (triangle groups Γ_{p,q}, Γ_{∞,3}=PSL(2,Z), curves C_{pq}, normalizers Norm(π)/π) shows the purpose. This is the topological set-up for treating modular curves and their covers as orbifolds (the 'multiplicités modulaires' viewpoint). The fundamental group of the stacky quotient of the upper half-plane by a Fuchsian group is then that group itself, since the upper half-plane is contractible.
errors: No mathematical errors. Uniqueness of B 'à isomorphisme unique près' holds when B is taken together with its universal covering class, which the context implies. The '=1' under π_0(X) indicates the connected case, in which the sequence becomes a short exact extension.
